name: Structural Equivalence and Efficiency in Grammar-Constrained Decoding
executive_summary: Formal analysis of when two different grammar-constrained decoding implementations produce equivalent output distributions, and how to make constrained decoding more efficient.
description: Extends the grammar-constrained decoding line of work (see structured-output-json-mode) with a formal treatment of structural equivalence between decoding implementations and efficiency improvements to the constraint-checking process itself. Downstream, follow-on research rather than the foundational paper.
when_to_use: Implementing or evaluating a grammar-constrained decoding system where correctness/equivalence guarantees matter, not just a single reference implementation.
when_not_to_use: Using an off-the-shelf structured-output feature without needing to reason about implementation-level equivalence.

primary_source.title: Structural Equivalence and Efficiency in Grammar-Constrained LLM Decoding

variables.description: The formal grammar constraining valid output

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
